about.title: Norwalk Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Falls rarely make the news the way traffic collisions do, even in a year when Norwalk recorded 413 injury collisions, yet a wet aisle or a loose stair tread can leave someone with an injury just as lasting. Along Rosecrans Avenue, Imperial Highway, and Pioneer Boulevard, people move through grocery stores, strip-mall parking lots, restaurants, and medical offices every day, and each of those properties is expected to be kept reasonably safe for visitors. When an owner in this part of Los Angeles County knew about a hazard, or should have noticed it with ordinary attention, and did nothing to fix it or warn people, California law allows the injured person to seek compensation. That is the core of a premises liability claim. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Norwalk residents with an independent attorney who takes these cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless money is recovered. You concentrate on healing while the attorney deals with the property owner and its insurer.

whyChoose.title: Why Norwalk Residents Use LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Proving the owner had notice
items.desc: In California, the injured person generally has to show the owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it. The attorney you are matched with knows how to gather cleaning logs, inspection records, and witness accounts that speak to that question.

items.title: Deadlines that differ by property
items.desc: Most California premises claims must be filed within two years, but a fall on property owned by a public entity involves a much shorter claim window. Getting connected early helps ensure the right deadline is identified and met.

items.title: Comparative fault doesn't end a claim
items.desc: California applies pure comparative fault, so a claim can move forward even if you are found partly responsible, with the recovery reduced by your share. An independent attorney can push back when an insurer tries to pin most of the blame on you.

items.question: I fell at a store off Imperial Highway and didn't take pictures. Is my claim over?
items.answer: No. Photos help, but they are not the only evidence. Most retail properties in Norwalk have surveillance cameras, and footage is often overwritten within days or weeks, so an attorney will typically send a preservation request right away. Incident reports, receipts showing you were there, and statements from anyone who saw the hazard can also fill in the picture.

items.question: What if the fall happened on city or county property in Norwalk?
items.answer: Claims against a public entity in California follow a separate process with a much shorter deadline than the usual two years, and a formal government claim generally has to be filed first. Sidewalks, civic buildings, parks, and transit facilities can all raise this issue. Because the timeline is so compressed, it is worth speaking with an attorney as soon as you can.

items.question: The property owner says I should have been watching where I was walking. Does that matter?
items.answer: It can affect the amount, but not whether you can bring a claim. California uses pure comparative fault, meaning any percentage assigned to you reduces your recovery rather than eliminating it. Attorneys in the LawProactive network work on contingency, so you can have that argument evaluated without paying anything up front.
